items.title: Delhi High Court asks police to decide bank union's plea for protest site by September 28
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday directed the Delhi Police to take a decision by September 28 on a government bank employees' union request for a site to protest in the national capital. Justice Amit Mahajan said that the decision should be communicated to the union. "Respondent authorities are directed to consider the request for an alternate site to hold a demonstration by Monday," the Court said. Justice Amit Mahajan, Delhi High Court The Court passed the order while dealing with a plea filed by United Forum of Bank Unions Delhi State (UFBU). Bank employees have called a 3-day nationwide strike from September 28 to 30, seeking implementation of a 5-day banking week. They are also seeking reconsideration of the Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. UFBU had approached the High Court seeking permission to hold a peaceful dharna at Jantar Mantar on September 28, 29 and 30. The petition challenged the police's denial and delay in granting permission for the proposed demonstrations. They said that if permission to protest at Jantar Mantar cannot be given, they should be allowed to hold the dharna at an alternate location. items.summary: At least two journalists covering a protest against the Election Commission of India at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on Friday alleged that they were forcibly detained and manhandled by Delhi Police personnel. One reporter said his microphone was snatched and broken and another alleged that a policeman dragged him away from the protest site and asked him to delete photographs. Civil society groups and activists organised the protest, and the All India Students’ Association joined it. items.title: Women wrestlers move sessions court against Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh's acquittal in sexual harassment case
items.summary: Four women wrestlers have approached a sessions court challenging the acquittal of Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in the sexual harassment case. The appeal against the magistrate court's order of August 3 is likely to be heard by the sessions judge on Saturday. Notably, the women wrestlers have also challenged the acquittal of co-accused Vinod Tomar in the case. Wrestlers say the trial court order is based on "surmises and conjectures" and its reasoning is based on "archaic and stereotypical assumptions" about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment. It has been stated that the trial court fixated on small, unimportant slips and used them to reject the case against Singh in its entirety, instead of looking at the whole picture backed up by witness corroboration. The case pertains to sexual harassment allegations raised by six women wrestlers against Singh. Based on their complaints, the police had registered a first information report (FIR) against the MP. items.title: Collegium should include President’s nominee, Attorney General: Retired Justice Pankaj Mithal
items.summary: The Supreme Court collegium should be expanded to include a nominee of the President of India, the Attorney General for India and an independent constitutional functionary to improve transparency and restore public confidence in judicial appointments, former Supreme Court Justice Pankaj Mithal said on Thursday. Speaking in Hindi, at the fifth edition of Nyay Nirman @ 2047: Building the Legal Architecture of India’s Global Future , Justice Mithal said reform of the judicial appointments process was among the most urgent changes required as India looks towards becoming a developed nation by 2047. “ However, we must candidly acknowledge that the Collegium system is an extra-constitutional authority that we created. While it was established with good intentions, it now requires substantial improvement, ” he said. Justice Mithal proposed expanding the Supreme Court collegium to seven members.
